title: Musa was given a complete Book, as a reward for doing good.
subtitle: The Tawrah: detail, guidance, mercy
then: Right after the straight path, Allah praises the Tawrah. Ibn Kathir notes {idea}Allah often mentions the Quran and the Tawrah together.{/idea} The Book was complete for Musa's law and given {reward}as a reward for his doing right and obeying{/reward}, citing: is the reward for good anything but good?
now: You worked carefully, honestly, kept your promises, and then a door opened. {reward}That is often how Allah works: good answered with more good.{/reward} {idea}Keep doing your best quietly. It is being noticed.{/idea}
old: Doing good rarely gets me anywhere.
new: Allah answers good with good. The gift often follows the effort.
try: Do one task today with full care and excellence, even if no one checks it.

title: This Book is blessed. Follow it, and mercy follows you.
subtitle: The Quran as Allah's firm rope
then: After the Tawrah, the Quran: {reward}a blessed Book, so follow it and be mindful of Allah, that you may receive mercy.{/reward} Ibn Kathir says Allah tells His servants to {idea}understand it, hold to it, and call others to it{/idea}, because it is the firm rope of Allah, blessed for whoever acts on it.
now: There is a beautiful mushaf in your house, wrapped in cloth on a high shelf. It gets dusted more than it gets opened. {idea}The blessing is in following it, not keeping it safe.{/idea}
old: Having the Quran in my home brings blessing on its own.
new: The Quran's blessing reaches me when I read it and follow it.
try: Take the Quran down today and read one page, then pick one line to act on.

title: No more saying: the Book was not sent to us.
subtitle: The Quran removes the excuse of not knowing

row.title: it is not in my language

then: Ibn Abbas said the two groups were the Jews and Christians. Ibn Jarir explained the Quran came so the Arabs could not say: {trap}we did not understand their books, it was not our language, we were busy and unaware.{/trap} {idea}Now a Book had come to them in their own tongue.{/idea}
now: "I do not understand Arabic." "I never had a teacher." Yet translations sit in your phone in your language, with audio, for free. {idea}The excuse of distance is gone.{/idea} The Book was sent to you too.
old: I cannot really understand the Quran, so it is not for me.
new: The Quran was sent so no one could say it never reached them. It reached me.
try: Open a translation in your own language and read five verses with full attention.

title: We would be better guided, they said. Now proof came.
subtitle: The boast answered by a clear sign

row.title: if only we had a Book
I have it now
sub: what am I doing with it?

then: The Arabs had sworn that if a warner came they would be {trap}more guided than any nation.{/trap} The reply: {reward}a clear proof, guidance and mercy have come to you.{/reward} As-Suddi explained the word for turning away as hindering others from it; Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and Qatadah said it means turning away.
now: "If I lived near a great mosque I would go every day." "If I had more time I would learn." {trap}The if-only version of you is always better.{/trap} {idea}The real test is what you do with what you already have.{/idea}
old: If I had better circumstances, I would be much more devoted.
new: Guidance is already in my hands. The question is what I do with it now.
try: Pick one if-only you often say. Do a small version of it today with what you have.

title: When certain signs arrive, late faith no longer helps.
subtitle: Waiting until it is too late to turn
then: The deniers kept delaying, as if waiting for angels or for Allah to come. Ibn Kathir cites the hadith in Bukhari: {trap}the Hour will not come until the sun rises from the west; when people see it, all will believe, but then faith will not help one who did not believe before.{/trap} {idea}Faith and good deeds must come before that.{/idea}
now: "I will get serious after the wedding." "After the kids are older." "When I retire." {trap}Every delay assumes the door stays open.{/trap} {idea}Today it is open.{/idea}
old: I will turn to Allah properly once life settles down.
new: There is a point where turning back stops counting. Today is not that day.
try: Make sincere tawbah today for one thing you have been saving for later.

title: Those who split their religion into camps: you are not of them.
subtitle: The Prophet ﷺ kept clear of division
then: Several early scholars said this was about earlier communities who split into sects. Ibn Kathir says it {idea}applies to all who divide the religion{/idea} into camps of opinion and desire, since the law Allah sent is one. He cites the hadith: {reward}we prophets are brothers, and our religion is one.{/reward} Their matter is left to Allah.
now: Two mosques in the same town that do not greet each other. A group chat that turns every topic into a fight between labels. {trap}You start loving your camp more than your Lord.{/trap} {idea}Hold the path, and leave the scoring of others to Allah.{/idea}
old: Defending my group against other Muslims is defending the religion.
new: Splitting the religion into camps is something the Prophet ﷺ stood apart from.
try: Greet or thank someone this week from a Muslim group you usually avoid.

title: One good deed counts ten. One bad deed counts one.
subtitle: How generously Allah keeps the record

row.title: a good intention is written
sub: and a sin left for Allah too

then: Ibn Kathir cites the hadith from Ibn Abbas: {reward}whoever intends a good deed and does not do it, it is written as one good deed; if he does it, ten up to seven hundred and more.{/reward} Whoever intends a sin and leaves it for Allah's sake, that too is written as good. {idea}If he does it, one sin, unless Allah erases it.{/idea}
now: You meant to visit your sick aunt but the day ran out. You were about to send the angry text, then deleted it. {reward}Both were noticed and written.{/reward} {idea}Allah keeps your record more generously than you keep your own.{/idea}
old: My bad deeds outweigh everything good I try to do.
new: Allah multiplies my good and counts my bad only once. Even my intentions count.
try: Intend three good deeds this morning. Do at least one before sunset.

title: My Lord guided me: the upright way of Ibrahim.
subtitle: A firm religion, easy and pure
then: After all the arguments with the idolaters, the Prophet ﷺ is told to declare: {idea}my Lord has guided me to a straight path, a firm religion, the way of Ibrahim, upright.{/idea} Ibn Kathir cites Ibn Abbas: the Prophet ﷺ was asked which religion Allah loves most, and said {reward}the upright, easy way.{/reward}
now: Someone tells you faith is a burden that makes life heavy. {reward}The Prophet ﷺ described it as upright and easy.{/reward} {idea}Ibrahim's way was simple: turn to Allah alone and walk straight.{/idea}
old: Being religious means making life harder for myself.
new: The way of Ibrahim is upright and easy: Allah alone, and a straight walk.
try: Say today, from the heart: my Lord has guided me. Thank Him for it once.

title: My prayer, my sacrifice, my life and my death: all for Allah.
subtitle: One sentence that covers everything
then: The idolaters prayed to idols and sacrificed to them. The Prophet ﷺ is told to declare the opposite: {idea}my prayer and my rites are for Allah alone.{/idea} Ibn Kathir says Allah commanded him to {reward}dedicate his intention and heart sincerely to Him.{/reward} Then the circle widens to his whole life and death.
now: You pray at 1 p.m. and then walk back into a meeting as if Allah stayed on the mat. {idea}This verse puts the commute, the work, the dinner table, and the last breath in the same sentence as prayer.{/idea}
old: My religious life and my normal life are two separate things.
new: My prayer, my work, my whole life and my death can all be for Allah.
try: Before you start work today, quietly say this verse's meaning: this too is for You.

title: He has no partner. I was commanded this, and I submit first.
subtitle: The one who calls is the first to obey
then: Qatadah said {idea}first of the Muslims means the first of this ummah{/idea}, since all prophets before called to Islam. Ibn Kathir lists Nuh, Ibrahim, Yusuf, Musa and the disciples of Isa, each saying they were Muslims, meaning {reward}they submitted to Allah alone.{/reward}
now: You tell your kids to put their phones down at dinner while yours is in your hand. {idea}The Prophet ﷺ was the first to do what he called others to.{/idea} The one who calls goes first.
old: It is enough to tell others what is right.
new: The Prophet ﷺ was first to submit. I start with myself before I tell others.
try: Pick one piece of advice you give others often. Do it yourself today first.

title: No one carries another's load. Each soul earns for itself.
subtitle: Why look for any other lord?
then: The Prophet ﷺ asks: {idea}shall I seek a lord other than Allah, when He is Lord of all things?{/idea} Ibn Kathir says this verse is about trusting Him, after the last one was about worshipping Him, like "You alone we worship, You alone we ask for help." Then: {reward}no soul carries another's burden{/reward}, a sign of His perfect justice.
now: You grew up hearing your family's mistakes would follow you. Or you secretly hope your parents' prayers will cover your own neglect. {reward}Neither is true.{/reward} {idea}You are not your father's sins, and you are not saved by your mother's tahajjud.{/idea}
old: I am stuck with what my family did, or covered by what they did.
new: I carry my own deeds. That is fair, and it means my path is mine to walk.
try: Put down one guilt that belongs to someone else, and pick up one good deed that is yours.

title: Placed on earth, ranked differently, and tested in what you were given.
subtitle: The surah closes with warning and mercy together
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah made people differ in {idea}provision, character, looks and color{/idea} to test them: the rich in how they thank, the poor in how they are patient. The surah ends: swift in penalty, and {reward}Forgiving, Merciful.{/reward} He closes with the hadith: {reward}My mercy overcomes My anger.{/reward}
now: Your colleague earns double. Your neighbor's kids got into the good school. You compare all day. {idea}Their portion is their test. Yours is yours.{/idea} {reward}And the One running the test has mercy that outweighs His anger.{/reward}
old: What I have compared to others shows what I am worth.
new: What I was given is my test, not my score. And His mercy is greater than His anger.
try: Name one thing you have more of than others and one you have less of. Thank Allah for the first, and be patient with the second.
